<action type="say">
Because the ticket was booked directly on Frontier’s site, I can’t access or cancel it from this system; only Frontier (or your Frontier account) can modify that booking.

Since the flight has already departed and you didn’t take it, Frontier will almost always treat this as a “no‑show,” which typically means:
- The value of the ticket is forfeited, and  
- No refund or travel credit is issued, unless:
  - You canceled/changed it before departure, or  
  - You bought a fare bundle or travel insurance that specifically covers this.

Here’s what you can still do in a few minutes:

1) Check your booking/Frontier account  
   - Go to flyfrontier.com → “My Trips.”  
   - Enter the confirmation code BK-F94402-20260902 and your last name: Park.  
   - See if the trip shows as “completed,” “no‑show,” or if there is any note of travel credit.

2) Look for any credits or vouchers  
   - If you have a Frontier account, sign in and check “Credits/Vouchers” or “My Wallet” for any remaining value.  
   - Also check your email (including spam/junk) around the travel date for any message about a credit or change.

3) If you think you had a more flexible fare or insurance  
   - If you purchased “The WORKS,” “The PERKS,” or third‑party travel insurance, review those terms; they may allow partial refund or credit even if you didn’t fly.  
   - Then contact Frontier support (chat or phone) and reference your confirmation code to ask if any residual value can be recovered.

If you tell me:
- What fare/bundle you remember buying (Basic vs. WORKS/PERKS), and  
- Whether you canceled or tried to change it before departure,  
I can give you a more precise expectation of whether any money might still be recoverable.</action>
